_about: Published score distributions for the UAT-UK admissions tests. Every figure here was read off an official UAT-UK technical report; nothing is estimated, interpolated or inferred. Percentiles are of the SCALED (1-9) score, not of raw marks — no raw-to-scale conversion table has ever been published for TMUA or ESAT in any year.
_use: These are the TARGET end of an equating: they describe today's curve. The source end — a raw mark's standing in its own year's cohort — is NOT available for most papers. See _gaps.

_gaps.raw_to_scale_tables: None exist, for any test, in any year. Confirmed by enumerating every PDF on the archived Cambridge Assessment Admissions Testing site and the UAT-UK bucket. Anything circulating as a 'TMUA score conversion table' is a tutoring company's reconstruction, not an official document, and is not used here.
_gaps.engaa_nsaa_statistics: No mean, SD, median, quartile or candidate count was ever published for ENGAA or NSAA, in any year. Explanation-of-Results documents exist only for November 2021 and November 2023, and both give distributions as unlabelled bar charts with no numbers on them.
_gaps.tmua_2016_2023: Distributions published as unlabelled charts only. No summary statistics in any year.
_gaps.consequence: Telos cannot honestly equate an ENGAA, NSAA or pre-2024 TMUA raw mark onto today's scale from published data alone. The intended route is Telos's own cohort once enough students have logged these papers — the same idea as the planned percentile phase.

_scale_regimes._note: The 1-9 scale is norm-referenced and has been re-anchored four times, so a scaled score means nothing without knowing which regime issued it. Quotes are the awarding body's own wording.
_scale_regimes.TMUA 2016: approximately 50% of candidates will achieve overall scores higher than 5.0 ... approximately 10% of applicants will achieve overall scores higher than 7.5
_scale_regimes.TMUA 2017-2023: approximately one third of candidates will achieve overall scores higher than 6.5. High scores are capped at 9.0.
_scale_regimes.ENGAA/NSAA: typical applicants will score around 4.0. Approximately 10% of applicants will achieve scores higher than 7.0. Low scores are capped at 1.0.
_scale_regimes.TMUA/ESAT 2024 onward: typical candidates will score around 4.5. Approximately 10% of candidates will achieve scores higher than 7.0. Low scores are capped at 1.0 and high scores are capped at 9.0.

_cross_year_warning: The awarding body explicitly disclaims cross-year comparison. TMUA October 2024 Explanation of Results: 'This scaling process has been revised for 2024/25, and scores should not be compared directly with TMUA scores from earlier years.' ESAT 2025-26 Technical Report: 'as the scaling is calculated independently for each admissions cycle, the scaled score summaries cannot be directly compared across admissions cycles.' This is the reason Telos equates rather than compares.
